children: Following a strategic review, the board of CooperCompanies
has decided to maintain its ownership of CooperSurgical rather than sell the division.

"The Board believes certain temporary factors impacted the perceived valuation at the end of the process, including recent updates regarding a competitive entrant to the non-hormonal IUD market and the impact of the Company’s recent fertility litigation settlement," the company said in a
. "The Board and its advisors believe these items contributed to a valuation disconnect whereby offers received were not in the best interest of shareholders.
In addition, Cooper boosted its share buyback authorization to $3B from $2B.
In after-hours trading, however, the company best known for contact lenses is down ~13% after issuing fiscal 2026 Q3 results that included guidance revisions

FY 2026 revenue guidance of $4.229B-$4.252B (from $4.285B-$4.321B prior) is below the consensus of $4.31B. Non-GAAP diluted EPS is seen at $4.51-$4.55 ($4.58-$4.66 prior), which is below the consensus of $4.63.
In FQ3, the company missed on the top line but beat on the top.
Cooper ended FQ3 (ended July 31) with cash and cash equivalents of $154.7M compared to $110.6M on Oct. 31, 2025.

title: CooperCompanies keeping CooperSurgical; shares drop on updated guidance
